source.title: Minimum Deletions to Make Array Beautiful

teaching.hint: As you scan the original order, what information determines the next kept element’s role?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The constraint is on adjacent pairs in the retained sequence; a kept-count parity and the open pair’s first value suffice.
solution_outline.approach: Scan left to right. Keep each candidate opener; keep a closer when it differs from the opener, otherwise delete it. At the end, delete any unmatched opener.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every completed retained pair is valid. When a candidate equals the open value, keeping it cannot close that pair; the first different candidate closes it at the earliest possible position.
solution_outline.correctness: For each pair, choosing the earliest possible different closer leaves at least as much suffix for later pairs as any alternative. A trailing unmatched opener cannot remain in an even-length result.
solution_outline.pitfall: Original-index parity is irrelevant after deletions; an unmatched final opener still costs one deletion.

common_wrong_turns: Checking original instead of surviving indices
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained deletion order, empty-array validity, and survivor-index semantics.
